cur-legend-arthur.dateNote: First named in Welsh sources written some three centuries after the period he is said to belong to. No contemporary evidence of him survives, and Tintagel is tradition rather than proof.

cur-legend-merlin.dateNote: A literary figure assembled by Geoffrey of Monmouth in the 1130s from earlier Welsh poetry. The link to Carmarthen rests on the similarity of the names.

cur-legend-robinhood.dateNote: First appears in ballads from the 1300s, and is traditionally placed in the reign of Richard I. No outlaw of the name has been identified in the records of the time.

cur-dis-fire-london.placeNote: Shown at Pudding Lane, where the fire started in a bakery on 2 September 1666. It went on to burn most of the walled city.
